extracted.intended_audience: General readers interested in BBC Verify, journalism, and fact-checking
extracted.subtask_description: Describes the practices, methods, formats, and observed sourcing/content patterns of BBC Verify (the BBC's fact‑checking unit) and its Verify Live product. Useful for understanding how a news organization conducts verification and how its output has been evaluated by researchers and regulators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of OSINT, satellite imagery, data analysis and forensic techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: BBC describes BBC Verify as "a specialist team of journalists using open-source intelligence (OSINT), satellite imagery, data analysis and forensic techniques."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These methods are the stated toolset for verification work. They imply reliance on publicly available digital evidence, geospatial imagery, quantitative analysis, and forensic review of media to establish facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core verification functions (fact-checking, video verification, countering disinformation, data analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: BBC Verify "fact-check[s] information, verify[ies] video, counter[s] disinformation, and analyse[s] data to separate fact from fake, and to bring clarity on complex issues."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose-driven criteria: outputs should check factual claims, authenticate video, identify/disrupt disinformation narratives, and use data analysis to clarify complex topics. Work should aim to separate fact from falsehood and clarify complexity for audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency / explainability of verification ('pulls back the curtain')
rubrics_metrics.description: BBC Verify says that it "pulls back the curtain" to show not only news, but to verify how it has come to be known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verification outputs are expected to show methods and reasoning (how conclusions were reached). The original site provides individual entries per story, which supports traceability and explainability of verification steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live/cumulative verification format (BBC Verify Live)
rubrics_metrics.description: In 2025 BBC Verify Live was added, described as "a single page on the BBC News home page and on the BBC app for a day with verification of many of the day's news stories added cumulatively as available."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a product/format standard: present multiple verifications centrally with updates added throughout the day. Implies timeliness, iterative updates, and a single consolidated UI for daily verification work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sourcing practice: heavy reliance on official/governmental corroborating sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers found that Verify Live used "official governments and their militaries or agencies as well over three-quarters of main corroborating sources, with comparatively limited use of think tanks, policy institutes, nongovernmental organisations, experts, academics or eyewitnesses."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identifies an observed sourcing standard/pattern: preference for official/agency sources as primary corroboration. Guidance/implication: source diversity (including independent experts, NGOs, eyewitness accounts) is comparatively limited and may affect perspectives and independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical emphasis: focus on foreign affairs over domestic politics
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers reported that Verify "heavily emphasised foreign affairs, and argued that it could and should be used more to fact-check UK politics," with an exception for some major political developments and the runup to the 2024 general election when politicians' claims were checked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coverage selection is a criterion: current practice prioritizes international/foreign affairs verification. Recommendation/implicit standard: consider broader application to domestic political claims, particularly during high-stakes political periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public uptake and recognition as a usage metric
rubrics_metrics.description: According to Ofcom (Nov 2024) "26% of UK adults said they had used a fact-checking website or tool at least once, with BBC Verify most likely to be used and heard of; one in five said they used it at least once, and one in twenty saying they do so regularly."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides an evaluative metric for the service: public awareness and self-reported use frequency. Useful for measuring reach, trust, and audience engagement with fact-checking services.
